items.title: Live: Trump says he 'doesn't care' if Iran comes back for ceasefire talks as blockade looms
items.description: US Central Command say it will begin implementing a blockade of "all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports" from midnight tonight AEST. Follow live.

items.title: The US will cut off the Strait of Hormuz. Here's what the blockade means
items.description: US president Donald Trump has ordered his nation's military to cut off all Iranian ports from maritime traffic passing through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most vital shipping routes.

items.title: Trump criticises Pope Leo, extending feud over Iran war
items.description: Writing on social media after the pope called for peace, US President Donald Trump says the first American pope is "terrible for foreign policy" and he should "stop catering to the Radical Left".

items.title: Booking.com customers involved in possible data and security breach
items.description: Some Booking.com customers are being warned their personal information may have been accessed by unauthorised third parties, prompting fresh concerns about the security of travellers' data.

items.title: Albanese names new defence force chief
items.description: Vice Admiral Mark Hammond, who has spent 40 years in the navy, will replace current defence force chief David Johnston when he retires in July.

items.title: How did a 3km hike go so wrong? Retracing Celine Cremer's final steps
items.description: Belgian backpacker Celine Cremer was on the trip of a lifetime, but on a hike in Tasmania she left the trail and was never seen again. It took a private investigator, a YouTuber, loved ones and an army of volunteers to find answers.

items.title: Canada has flipped the script on child care. Could Australia copy?
items.description: Australia definitely won't nationalise child care, even though the data suggests there's a strong case. Perhaps a more feasible idea would be to copy what Canada has done.

items.title: Underground 3D printing farms arming Ukraine's soldiers
items.description: In spare rooms and backyard sheds, volunteers across Europe are 3D printing drone bomb parts to supply Ukraine's military.

items.title: 'Like a flea on an elephant's back': The unexpected rise of solar power
items.description: Solar power is forecast to overtake coal as the world's biggest source of electricity next year, and its growth shows no signs of slowing down. Behind its success is a little-known Australian inventor.

items.title: Live: ASX slips as oil surges back above $US100 on US threat of Gulf blockade
items.description: Failed US-Iran peace talks send oil prices surging higher and the Australian share market lower. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Record attendance for AFL Gather Round as premier warns of 'lite' interstate version
items.description: South Australia's premier says he is "trying to hold the line" as Gather Round negotiations continue, with the 2026 event attracting record crowds.

items.title: Rory McIlroy joins exclusive group with second straight Masters victory
items.description: Rory McIlroy becomes just the fourth man in history to win back-to-back Masters titles after holding off a star-studded field in the final round at Augusta. Follow live.

items.title: Man agrees he tried to 'humiliate' prominent surfer before fatal assault
items.description: A man has admitted to stripping a prominent Sydney surfer naked and shaking him by his ankles in an attempt to humiliate him before causing his unlawful death.

items.title: Memorial for women allegedly killed by men removed from Melbourne laneway
items.description: The founder of Australian Femicide Watch says she is heartbroken over the removal of the She Matters mural in Hosier Lane dedicated to more than 200 women who have died since January 2025.

items.title: How to make your workplace dog-friendly
items.description: How can employers design dog-friendly workplaces if they want to, and what does the law say about animals at work?

items.title: How recycling can help solve a 'huge issue' in tennis
items.description: What should be done with all those used tennis balls that get inevitably sent to landfill? Lilian Xu might have found the answer.

items.title: Quiz: Jump in, we're going back in time
items.description: Which state had Australia's only communist MP? And where did the Titanic sink?

items.title: Shock loss of Emily has friends saying 'get your moles checked'
items.description: Emily avoided the sun and "did everything right". No-one considered that a melanoma removed from her shoulder in 2022 had spread to her brain.

items.title: Health minister and veteran MPs step down before Victorian state election
items.description: Long serving Labor MPs Mary-Anne Thomas, Danny Pearson and Gayle Tierney have announced they will not contest the 2026 state election.

items.title: Farmer braces for backlash after speaking up in support of transmission lines
items.description: A farmer in Victoria's north is offering up his property for transmission lines as part of the VNI West project, saying it would give him a chance to diversify his income.

items.title: Children and 75yo among dozens of homeless in major holiday town
items.description: A homeless survey conducted in one of WA's best-known holiday hotspots uncovers dozens of people sleeping rough, including a 75-year-old.

items.title: Borlase leads host of Opals stars to sign new WBA free agency deals
items.description: Izzy Borlase is rewarded for her MVP-winning season with the Bendigo Spirit as she pens a new deal with the Atlanta Dream in the WNBA.

items.title: 'Coddled' and 'dangerously unchallenged': What experts say about Kim Jong Un's daughter
items.description: North Korea leader Kim Jong Un's 13-year-old daughter is tipped to be next in line. So who is Kim Ju Ae?

items.title: Trump ally Viktor Orbán concedes 'painful' defeat in Hungary election
items.description: After 16 years in power, the powerful far-right leader says he will serve in opposition, with centre-right ⁠candidate Péter Magyar's Tisza Party ​on course for a super majority.

items.title: Nigerian military air strike on market reportedly kills more than 100 civilians
items.description: Amnesty International calls for an independent investigation into an air strike on a Nigerian market, where the country's military says it was targeting militants.
